chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahboub from Al-Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Al-Hajjal from Al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Everything was water, and His Throne was upon the water. So Allah, Exalted is His mention, commanded the water, and it ignited into fire. Then He commanded the fire, and it was extinguished, and from its smoldering smoke arose. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the heavens from that smoke, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the earth from the ashes. Then the water, the fire, and the wind contended. The water said,
I am the greatest army of Allah.
I am the greatest army of Allah.
I am the greatest army of Allah.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the wind:
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia Islamic narrative regarding the creation of the heavens and earth from water and fire?
ai.summary: This cosmological narrative from al-Kafi highlights the primordial role of water (al-Ma') in Shia thought, detailing the elemental transformation from water to fire, smoke, and ash to form the heavens and earth. It concludes with a unique theological contest among the elements, where Allah designates the wind (al-Rih) as His 'greatest army,' emphasizing divine sovereignty over natural forces. This account complements the concept of the Throne (Al-Arsh) resting upon water, a key motif in Islamic cosmology found in both Quran and Hadith.
